description: AI/ML framework matrix and LLM engine APIs. Maps each framework's GPU compute path, quantization support, and porting implications.

gpu_backends.cuda: ATen kernels compiled via `python setup.py` or pip torch+cu126. Custom kernels via Triton.
gpu_backends.hip: ROCm-torch (pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm6.0). Custom C++ extensions via hipify.
gpu_backends.vulkan: No native Vulkan backend. Use TorchInductor → C++ path with vulkan-compute in Rust, or use ExecuTorch Vulkan delegate.
gpu_backends.xpu: Intel PyTorch (oneAPI) — for Intel Arc GPUs via SYCL

triton_support.cuda: Full — torch._inductor codegen uses Triton for CUDA kernels
triton_support.hip: Full (since PyTorch 2.4, PR #121801). PyTorch CI now pulls from openai/triton main repo (third_party/amd).

quantization.bitsandbytes: CUDA only — NF4, FP4, INT8 (no AMD support)

porting_notes.AMD: Install: `pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/rocm6.0/`. Triton-AMD (upstream in triton-lang/triton/main/third_party/amd as of 2025). Custom kernels may need manual CUDA→HIP translation for ops Triton-AMD doesn't support yet.
porting_notes.NVIDIA: Standard pip install torch. Triton (openai/triton) for custom kernels (Python-like DSL, compiles to PTX via MLIR).
porting_notes.Intel: intel-extension-for-transformers (IPEX) for Arc GPU. Or use SYCL via torch-xpu / oneAPI.
porting_notes.Vulkan: Use ExecuTorch (PyTorch's edge framework) which has Vulkan compute backend with GL_EXT_integer_dot_product (DP4a) support. See `executorch` entry.

tensorflow.name: TensorFlow / Keras

quantization.aot: TensorFlow Lite with GPU delegate (Vulkan/Metal on Android, OpenGL elsewhere)

tensorflow.porting_notes: For LLM porting: use tf-keras with float8_e4m3 on newer GPUs. TFLite GPU delegates use Vulkan compute.

jax.name: JAX / Flax

gpu_backends.vulkan: No native support — XLA targets CUDA/HIP only

jax.porting_notes: JAX uses XLA Pjrt — kernels are generated per-arch. For custom kernels: use Triton (CUDA) or HSAIL (AMD). Pallas for low-level kernel definition.

llamacpp.name: llama.cpp

gpu_backends.hip: llama.cpp with -DBUILD_HIP=ON — Vulkan compute support coming
gpu_backends.vulkan: llama.cpp with -DBUILD_VULKAN=ON — Vulkan compute via Vulkan-Hpp

quantization.cuda: Custom CUDA kernels — mma, imad, shmem
quantization.hip: Custom HIP kernels — dot4, FMA chains, rocBLAS for dense
quantization.vulkan: Custom Vulkan compute shaders — uses @GLSL for kernel code, compiled to SPIR-V

llamacpp.vulkan_coop_matrix_note: Vulkan CooperativeMatrix (GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix) is BROKEN on AMD drivers. llama.cpp's Vulkan backend falls back to DP4a-style (shared_f32_4x8_f32 / spv_dp4) instructions for matmul on AMD. NVIDIA Vulkan drivers support CooperativeMatrix natively.

porting_notes.AMD_vulkan: Uses DP4a (spirv instruction) for matmul — not CooperativeMatrix. Check `llama-vulkan.cpp` for the fallback shader.
porting_notes.AMD_hip: Uses dot4 instructions (v_dot4_i32_i8 on gfx1030, packed dot4 on gfx1100+).
porting_notes.NVIDIA_cuda: Uses Tensor cores (mma.m16n8k8) for dense + imad for quantized.

gpu_backends.cuda: torch.compile or custom CUDA kernels via Triton
gpu_backends.vulkan: No native support — use llama.cpp or vLLM

triton_language.name: OpenAI Triton (Programming Language)
triton_language.description: Python-like DSL for writing GPU kernels. Compiles to PTX for NVIDIA, HIP for AMD (experimental).

gpu_backends.cuda: Full support — compiles to PTX via MLIR
gpu_backends.hip: Full (upstreamed as of 2025). Code in openai/triton/main/third_party/amd. PR #121801 in pytorch/pytorch uses upstream triton AMD backend.
gpu_backends.vulkan: Not supported — MLIR-Vulkan compute backend is experimental
gpu_backends.windows: triton-windows (triton-lang/triton-windows) — native Windows build. MSVC for NVIDIA, clang-cl for AMD.

windows_support.amd_windows: Supported via clang-cl backend (PR #179 merged Dec 2025). Uses TheRock for ROCm/PyTorch.
windows_support.nvidia_windows: Fully supported with MSVC. Bundled CUDA toolchain (PTXAS 12.8/12.9).

porting_notes.AMD: Triton-AMD now upstreamed in openai/triton/main/third_party/amd. PyTorch 2.7+ uses it directly (PR #121801). For extracting Triton kernels to standalone HIP C++: see cross_port_framework_extraction.md.
porting_notes.NVIDIA: Primary target. All Triton features supported.
porting_notes.Intel: SYCL backend via MLIR — experimental. Check https://github.com/openai/triton/tree/main/third_party/intel
porting_notes.Windows_AMD: Use triton-windows with clang-cl backend. Requires TheRock for ROCm/PyTorch.
porting_notes.Windows_NVIDIA: Use triton-windows. MSVC + bundled CUDA toolchain.
porting_notes.extraction_to_cpp: To extract a Triton kernel to standalone CUDA/HIP C++: compile with Triton JIT, then use Triton to LLVM pass to get LLVM IR, then use `triton-opt --convert-to-llvm` to get LLVM IR. Alternatively, analyze the Triton IR and manually translate blocksize/warp patterns to CUDA/HIP intrinsics.

triton_language.torch_integration: torch.compile uses Triton for CUDA codegen (torch._inductor.triton). Windows requires triton-windows >= 3.1.

extraction_pattern.python_to_cpp: 1. Compile Triton kernel with triton.compile() → get PTX/AMDGCN binary. 2. Disassemble with cuobjdump/llvm-objdump. 3. Map PTX instructions to CUDA intrinsics or AMDGCN to HIP intrinsics. 4. Wrap in extern "C" function for C++ integration.
extraction_pattern.standalone_usage: Extracted kernels can be compiled standalone with nvcc/hipcc. No Python/Torch dependency at runtime.

executorch.name: ExecuTorch
executorch.description: PyTorch's edge deployment framework. Generates deployable ML models for mobile/embedded/IoT devices.

gpu_backends.hip: Not supported — no ROCm backend planned

quantization.vulkan: Vulkan compute — uses DP4a-style integer dot products (NOT CooperativeMatrix on AMD)

porting_notes.Vulkan_AMD: ExecuTorch's Vulkan backend uses shared_f32_4x8_f32 + spv_dp4 fallback (same pattern as llama.cpp). Verify GL_KHR_shader_integer_dot_product is enabled. IMPORTANT: Android NDK glslc doesn't support GL_EXT_integer_dot_product — use Vulkan SDK 1.4.321+ glslc instead (--target-env=vulkan1.3).
porting_notes.Vulkan_NVIDIA: Supports both DP4a (GL_EXT_integer_dot_product) and VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 (Vulkan 1.4.304 SDK).
porting_notes.Windows_DirectML: DirectML-EP via ONNX Runtime. Use DXC compiler + Agility SDK. DirectML is in sustained engineering — new work goes to Windows ML.
porting_notes.Windows_WindowsML: Windows ML (newer than DirectML) — WinML API with DirectML backend. Use for Windows 11+ deployments.
porting_notes.Windows_Triton: Combine ExecuTorch with triton-windows for custom CUDA kernels on Windows. Use Triton for CUDA compute, ExecuTorch Vulkan/DirectML for model orchestration.
porting_notes.Windows_AMD_Triton: Use triton-windows with clang-cl backend. Requires TheRock for ROCm/PyTorch. AMD support is newer (Dec 2025).

executorch.shader_extension_note: ExecuTorch PR #13743 added GL_EXT_integer_dot_product capability checking. Ensure Vulkan SDK 1.4.321+ and glslc with --target-env=vulkan1.3.

windows_triton_integration.use_case: Run custom CUDA/Triton kernels on Windows while using ExecuTorch's Vulkan/DirectML backend for model execution.
windows_triton_integration.setup: 1. pip install triton-windows. 2. pip install executorch[vulkan] or [directml]. 3. Export model with custom ops marked as Triton kernels. 4. Use Triton for CUDA backend, ExecuTorch for Vulkan/DX12 backend.
windows_triton_integration.note: Triton Windows is for CUDA kernels. For Vulkan kernels, use ExecuTorch's GLSL/SPIR-V backend directly.

torchinductor.name: TorchInductor
torchinductor.description: torch.compile backend. Generates fused kernels via Triton (CUDA) or C++ (CPU/HIP).

gpu_backends.hip: C++ codegen + hipify — generates HIP C++ kernels via `torch._inductor.codecache`
gpu_backends.vulkan: No native support — would need custom Vulkan codegen backend

torchinductor.porting_notes: For AMD: torchinductor hip path generates C++ kernels that require manual rocWMMA insertion for matmul ops. Triton codegen is CUDA-only.

vulkan_compute_rust.name: Vulkan Compute (Rust)
vulkan_compute_rust.description: Rust crate for Vulkan compute. Used by executorch, wgpu, and custom GPU compute projects.

gpu_backends.vulkan: Primary — uses ash/vulkano wsi for Vulkan compute

vulkan_compute_rust.porting_notes: Use `wgpu` for cross-platform compute. SPIR-V shaders compiled via glslangValidator or naga.

thunderkittens.name: ThunderKittens
thunderkittens.description: Tile-based GPU kernel primitives (16x16 matrix tiles at warp level). Matches or outperforms CuBLAS and FlashAttention-3. CUDA-focused with H100/B200 targets.

gpu_backends.hip: Reference: HipKittens (see separate entry) for AMD implementation
gpu_backends.vulkan: No direct support — tile primitives map to SPIR-V cooperative matrix

tiling_model.layout: Row/column major with matrix-core optimized layouts
tiling_model.async_ops: Async load/store across shared memory hierarchy

thunderkittens.porting_use_case: Use ThunderKittens kernels as performance references when porting. Compare your HIP/Vulkan implementation against TK's CUDA kernels.

hipkittens.name: HipKittens
hipkittens.description: AMD-focused tile-based kernel primitives (sister project to ThunderKittens). Targets CDNA3/CDNA4. Provides tile-based programming for AMD that carries over from TK's abstractions.

tiling_model.async_ops: Direct buffer loads to shared memory for latency hiding

hipkittens.porting_use_case: Use HipKittens as the AMD reference implementation. For porting CUDA→HIP: compare patterns — TK uses CUDA tiles, HK uses HIP tiles on wavefronts. Key differences: memory access patterns (coalesced vs bank-conflict-free), scheduling (warp vs wavefront), thread block ordering within chiplets. For RDNA (consumer GPUs): HK targets CDNA3/CDNA4 (wave64/wave32), but the tile abstractions, async load patterns, and scheduling strategies directly transfer — only the wavefront size (32 for RDNA vs 64 for CDNA) and LDS size differ. Use HK code as a starting template, then adjust: tile size (16x16 works for both), wavefront size (RDNA=32), and LDS size (RDNA1: 32KiB, RDNA2: 64KiB, RDNA3: 128KiB).
hipkittens.known_diff: TK→HK porting: tile primitives carry over, but memory scheduling and thread block ordering must be rethought for AMD chiplet architecture. Async load patterns differ due to different cache hierarchy.

tilelang.name: TileLang
tilelang.description: Tile-based programming DSL built on TVM IR. Generates optimized CUDA, HIP, Metal, CPU, and WebGPU code from a Pythonic tile-level API. Focuses on decoupling dataflow from scheduling (like Triton) but offers explicit hardware memory control (like ThunderKittens).

gpu_backends.hip: Full — generates HIP C++ targeting gfx90a/gfx1100/gfx1200/gfx1201

programming_model.scheduling: T.Pipelined(num_stages=N) for software pipelining, T.Parallel for elementwise

compilation_flow: 3. TVM IR lowering → TIR → target-specific codegen
tilelang.porting_use_case: TileLang kernels map tile primitives to hardware-specific instructions. Use T.alloc_shared for shared memory (matches CUDA __shared__, HIP __shared__). T.alloc_fragment maps to CUDA fragment registers or HIP accumulators. The scheduling primitives (num_stages, tile sizes) carry over directly — TileLang abstracts this across vendors.

comparison.thunderkittens: TK uses C++ templates, TileLang uses Python DSL with TVM backend. Both provide tile abstractions — TileLang covers more backends (HIP, Metal, WebGPU).
comparison.hipkittens: HK is C++ templates for AMD only. TileLang provides Python API targeting AMD via HIP codegen.
comparison.triton: Both use Python DSL. Triton hides thread/memory control. TileLang exposes hardware memory explicitly via T.alloc_shared/T.alloc_fragment.

known_limitations: TVM-based compilation can add overhead for simple kernels
NPU backend requires external Ascend project
No native Python callable at runtime (compiles to C++/CUDA/HIP)

openai_compatible.description: OpenAI API — chat completions, completions, embeddings

anthropic_compatible.description: Anthropic Claude API — messages, tools, thinking

mcp.description: Model Context Protocol — tool calling for AI agents
mcp.note: How K_and_S MCP server integrates — agents can query kands:// resources and call tools

vllm.description: vLLM — high-throughput inference server with PagedAttention, continuous batching

porting_notes.purpose: vLLM is the production-grade LLM inference server. tiny-vllm is a minimal educational reimplementation of vLLM's core ideas (PagedAttention, continuous batching, KV cache) in C++/CUDA.
porting_notes.cpu_port_notes: vLLM is CUDA-focused. CPU port would need to drop PagedAttention (GPU VRAM optimization), drop continuous batching (optional for CPU), and replace CUDA kernels with CPU BLAS. See tiny-vllm for the educational minimal version.

tiny_vllm.description: tiny-vllm — minimal educational LLM inference engine in C++/CUDA, sibling of vLLM
tiny_vllm.model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (safetensors, NOT included in repo — must be downloaded separately)

cpu_port_notes.bf16_on_cpu: No native BF16 on consumer Intel (10th-14th Gen). Options: software BF16 (slower), FP32 fallback (simplest), or ARM CPU with NEON BF16.
cpu_port_notes.cublas_replacement: Need CPU BLAS with BF16 or FP32 fallback. MKL (AVX-512_BF16 on 4th Gen Xeon+), OpenBLAS, Eigen (bfloat16 since 3.4), or FP32 BLAS.
cpu_port_notes.cuda_kernels_to_cpu: Most kernels are simple: embeddingGather (lookup loop), RMSNorm (dot product + scale), softmax (max-subtract). Attention is most complex but doable. PagedAttention can be dropped for CPU (contiguous KV cache).
cpu_port_notes.paged_attention_on_cpu: PagedAttention is a GPU VRAM optimization. On CPU with plenty of RAM, use contiguous KV cache. Drop PagedAttention entirely for CPU port.
cpu_port_notes.continuous_batching_on_cpu: Optional for CPU. For single-request CPU inference, drop continuous batching. Simpler.
cpu_port_notes.tokenizer: Uses HuggingFace transformers AutoTokenizer for 'meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct'. Need C++ tokenizer. Likely sentencepiece (LLaMA-style BPE). Check python/tokenizer.py.
cpu_port_notes.model_file: model.safetensors NOT in repo — must download from HuggingFace. ~2GB for BF16 1B model.
simplifications_for_cpu: Consider FP32 instead of BF16 (if no CPU BF16 support)
Drop HIP/CUDA dependencies (use CPU BLAS + CPU kernels)

files.main_cpp: src/main.cpp — main inference loop, weight loading, prefill, decode, batching (largest file)
files.kernels_cu: src/kernels.cu — CUDA kernels for all ops
files.cmakelists: CMakeLists.txt — CMake build with CUDA or HIP option
files.reference_txt: reference.txt — reference token IDs for verification
files.tokenizer_py: python/tokenizer.py — Python tokenizer script (uses transformers AutoTokenizer)
files.reference_py: python/reference.py — Python reference script (generates reference output?)

build.cmake: cmake . && make (or ninja), with CUDA toolkit or ROCm (USE_HIP=ON)
build.linux: Tested on Linux (6.19.8 x64_64) with CUDA Toolkit 13.1
build.windows: Not tested on Windows. Would need: CUDA toolkit for Windows, or HIP for Windows (AMD), or CPU BLAS for CPU port. CMake + MSVC or MinGW.
build.hip_option: USE_HIP=ON builds with HIP for AMD GPUs. hipBLAS instead of cuBLAS. hip::host + roc::hipblas.

triton_inference_server.description: NVIDIA Triton — model server with GPU scheduling

directml.porting_notes: DirectML uses DirectX 12 — requires DXC compiler + Agility SDK. Use GL_KHR_shader_integer_dot_product equivalent for matmul.

windows_ml.porting_notes: Uses DirectML under the hood. Best for ONNX models on Windows without CUDA.

nvidia_open_gpu_kernel_modules.description: NVIDIA Linux open GPU kernel module source (R515+) — open-source Linux kernel driver for NVIDIA GPUs
nvidia_open_gpu_kernel_modules.supported_gpus: Turing (RTX 20xx, GTX 16xx) and later; x86_64 or aarch64

porting_notes.Linux: Open-source kernel modules replace proprietary nvidia.ko. Requires GSP firmware from matching NVIDIA driver release (--no-kernel-modules flag). Use with DKMS for automatic rebuilds on kernel updates.
porting_notes.Windows: Not applicable — open kernel modules are Linux-only. Windows uses the proprietary driver.
porting_notes.Cross-vendor: Not relevant for CUDA/HIP porting itself, but relevant for Linux GPU driver development or UVM debugging. The open modules expose the same userspace ABI as proprietary driver.
porting_notes.relationship_to_cuda: CUDA still runs on top of this driver the same way — the userspace CUDA toolkit (nvidia-cuda-toolkit) does not change. This is a kernel-space change only.
porting_notes.gsp_note: Requires GSP (GPU System Processor) firmware from the matching driver release. Without it, the driver will not load on supported GPUs.

nvidia_open_gpu_doc.description: NVIDIA open GPU documentation — chip/hardware interface specs (power management, VRAM controller, GSP firmware interface)

porting_notes.purpose: Reference for anyone building Linux GPU drivers, kernel modules, or low-level GPU interfaces. Documents register layouts, power management, and hardware interfaces for NVIDIA GPUs.
porting_notes.relevance: Not directly relevant for CUDA/HIP kernel porting (that's userspace), but relevant for anyone working on Linux GPU driver support, VFIO, GPU passthrough, or comparing NVIDIA vs AMD kernel driver architectures.
porting_notes.vs_amd: AMD's equivalent is the AMDGPU kernel driver (in-tree Linux kernel) + command processor firmware (mesa/amd-pstate). NVIDIA's open kernel modules + open-gpu-doc are the closest NVIDIA equivalent.

gpuopen_isa_decoder.description: AMD GPUOpen IsaDecoder API — parse/decode AMD GPU instruction encodings from ISA XML
gpuopen_isa_decoder.endpoint: C++ library + headers (compile into your tool)

porting_notes.purpose: Parse AMD GPU ISA XML files and decode instruction encodings. Used by rocprof, llvm-objdump (with -mcpu), and custom tooling that needs to understand what an AMDGCN assembly blob actually says.
porting_notes.relevance: Relevant when you need to verify what instruction your HIP kernel actually compiled to — e.g. confirming v_dot4_i32_i8 vs v_dot4_i32_iu8 in the final binary, or checking that the compiler did not emit an unsupported encoding on gfx1031/gfx1201.
porting_notes.vs_nvidia: NVIDIA's ISA docs are PDF/PCIe-only (not machine-readable). The closest NVIDIA equivalent for instruction decoding is using cuobjdump --dump-sass + manual reading. For open parsing, NVIDIA's open-gpu-kernel-modules exposes some GPU interface but not a full ISA decoder like GPUOpen's IsaDecoder.
porting_notes.amd_isa_xml: Download ISA XML from https://gpuopen.com/machine-readable-isa/ — each file covers one arch + extension set. Update your local copy when targeting a new microarchitecture.

amd_gpuopen_isa.description: AMD GPUOpen — machine-readable GPU ISA XML for RDNA 1–4 and CDNA 1–5
supported_archs: gfx803 (Polaris/RX 580) — GCN 4 ISA, NOT in GPUOpen XML (use GCN 4 PDF manual)

not_in_xml.gfx803_Polaris: RX 580, RX 570, RX 480, RX 470, RX 460 — all Polaris (GCN 4th-gen). ISA XML does not exist. Use AMD GCN 4 ISA PDF manual.
not_in_xml.gcn_generations: GCN 1st (gfx600), 2nd (gfx700), 3rd (gfx801/gfx802), 4th (gfx803/gfx805), 5th (gfx900-series is RDNA, not GCN) — only RDNA 1 onwards is in the GPUOpen XML set. Earlier GCN uses PDF ISA manuals.

porting_notes.purpose: Machine-readable ISA reference — every AMD GPU instruction, its encoding, fields, operands, and availability by microarchitecture. This is the source of truth for what your HIP kernel can and cannot encode on a given arch.
porting_notes.usage: Use with isa_tools.py to probe whether a construct (v_dot4, mfma, wmma, etc.) actually encodes on the target arch. The IsaDecoder API (https://github.com/GPUOpen-Tools/isa_spec_manager) is the C++ parser for these XML files.
porting_notes.vs_nvidia: NVIDIA does not publish machine-readable ISA (PDFs only). For NVIDIA, you must use cuobjdump --dump-sass + manual reading, or rely on the PTX reference docs.
porting_notes.update_cycle: AMD releases new ISA XML files for each new microarchitecture. Keep a local copy per target arch; ISA XML for gfx1201/gfx1250 was added with RDNA4/CDNA4 support.

rx580_specific.isa_reference: AMD GCN 4 ISA manual (PDF) — not machine-readable, not in GPUOpen XML
rx580_specific.notes: RX 580 has no WMMA (no matrix cores). It has v_dot4_i32_i8 (4-way int8 dot product) and v_fma_f32 (fused multiply-add). It has 64 KiB LDS per CU. Wave size is 64. These features are documented in the GCN 4 ISA PDF, not in GPUOpen XML. If you need to verify encoding on RX 580, you are on your own with the PDF + objdump — there is no IsaDecoder XML for gfx803.

gtx1060_specific.isa_reference: NVIDIA Pascal PTX/SASS reference (PDF) — not machine-readable
gtx1060_specific.notes: GTX 1060 has no tensor cores (sm_70+ feature), no mma.sync, no WMMA. It has __shfl_sync, __ballot_sync, basic CUDA runtime API. CUDA still works on the proprietary NVIDIA driver — the lack of open kernel modules does not affect CUDA userspace. If porting to HIP, the HIP target arch (e.g. gfx1030, gfx1100) needs to support the translated HIP features — the GTX 1060 is the source, not the target.

model_format_quant_matrix.description: Which quant types work on which GPU backends

key.NVIDIA_CUDA: CUDA with tensor cores (sm_80+) or FP32 fallback (sm_75)
key.AMD_HIP: HIP with dot4 (RDNA2+) or FMA fallback
key.Intel_Ar: Intel Arc with DPAS and bf16/FP8 native
